sections.name: Bowser Space
sections.card:
Summary: At night in Party Mode the Donkey Kong Spaces of the day turn into Bowser Spaces, and landing on one makes Bowser hold a mini-game or a Bowser Bonus that can cost you coins, Orbs or a Star.
Weak points: Win the Bowser mini-game: Bowser takes coins or Orbs only from the players who lose and spares the winners. If you have no coins when you land, he gives you 10 coins and starts no mini-game or Bonus.
Tips: In the Bowser Bonus his special Dice Block can show 5, 10, 20 or 30 coins, or a Star, and he steals that much from the player who landed. If it shows a Star and you have none, he steals nothing. Clockwork Castle has no Bowser Spaces at all.

sections.name: DK Space
sections.card:
Summary: By day, the Donkey Kong Spaces on a Party Mode board bring Donkey Kong in for an event: a mini-game where players trade bananas for coins, or a DK Bonus for the player who landed.
Looks like: A yellow-orange space with Donkey Kong's face on it; Mario Party 6 is the only game where DK Spaces are yellow-orange instead of blue.
Tips: The DK Bonus uses a Dice Block shaped like a barrel, which can pay 5, 10, 20 or 30 coins or even a Star. At night every DK Space is replaced by a Bowser Space. Clockwork Castle has no DK Spaces, because Donkey Kong walks the board there.

sections.name: Chain Chomp
sections.card:
Summary: On Snowflake Lake, Chain Chomps live in the board's four doghouses, and a player who pays to ride one steals a Star from every rival it passes. Stars cannot be bought on this board.
Weak points: A Snack Orb protects you from one Chain Chomp theft: you throw a bone, the Chomp jumps over your space to catch it and carries on, and anyone else standing on your space is spared too. The Orb works only once. In a team game, teammates share Orbs and are not hurt by each other's traps, but a Chain Chomp ride by a teammate can still use up your Snack Orb.
Looks like: A black or dark blue metal ball with big round eyes, a wide mouth and sharp teeth, often bigger than Mario.
Tips: Each player starts with 5 Stars (more with a Star handicap), and a ride squishes teammates as well as rivals. A ride costs coins, and the price at night is not the same as by day.

sections.name: Pink Boo
sections.card:
Summary: A pink Boo who sells her stealing at night on Towering Treetop and Castaway Bay: pay 5 coins and she takes coins from a player, pay 40 and she takes a Star.
Weak points: A Boo-Away Orb stops her from stealing from you one time; it works on its own and cannot be used or placed. She only offers her services at night.
Looks like: A pink Boo, sometimes a light red one.
Tips: In this game she has taken over the job of the ordinary Boo, because Boo is now a playable character. The Boo-Away Orb is sold only on her two boards, for 10 coins.

sections.name: Evil Woody
sections.card:
Summary: At night the tree at the top of Towering Treetop is Evil Woody instead of Woody, and the ? Space beside him rains Spiny eggs that make every player lose coins, where Woody's daytime shower gives coins.
Weak points: When anyone lands on the ? Space at the top of the board at night, the Spiny eggs fall on every character and every player loses coins, not only the one who landed. By day the same space showers coins on everyone.
Looks like: A tree with a permanently angry face, blue with purple leaves, the opposite of Woody's colours.
Tips: Day turns into night every three turns, and a meter at the start of each turn shows how many are left, so you can time when to step onto that space.

sections.name: Whomp
sections.card:
Summary: Two Whomps stand in the way on Mario Party 6 boards, one on Snowflake Lake and one on Faire Square, and each lets you through only for 10 coins.
Weak points: He guards a path and asks for a toll: pay the 10 coins to get past.
Looks like: A large rectangular stone slab with an angry face, red eyes, a mouth with five uneven teeth, simple arms and legless feet.
Tips: On Snowflake Lake the Whomp stands in front of an Orb Shop, and passing takes you to the right side of the frozen pond. On Faire Square he sits in the middle of the board, and paying lets you quickly revisit Brighton or Twila for another chance to get Stars, which can save turns.

sections.name: Freezie
sections.card:
Summary: At night on Snowflake Lake, large Freezies appear and block the paths to the middle of the board, and they melt when daylight comes.
Weak points: Freezies block the paths to the middle of the board until daylight melts them, so plan to cross those paths when it is day.
Looks like: A large figure made entirely of ice, with a puzzled expression.
Tips: Day and night change every three turns, and the pause menu shows how many turns are left before the change. At night the ? Spaces beside the frozen pond start a snowball fight where players knock coins out of each other.

sections.name: Shadow Star Space
sections.card:
Summary: A space that hands you a Shadow Star, which takes away a Star, or coins if you have none. In Mario Party 6 it appears only in Castaway Bay and Clockwork Castle.
Weak points: On Castaway Bay it is Bowser's Battle Yacht, which swaps places with DK's Riverboat whenever someone stops on the riverboat, so check which boat is at the Star Space before you land.
Tips: The loss is 20 coins when you have no Star. On Clockwork Castle the Warp Pipes can get you away from Bowser.

sections.name: Bullet Bill Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A green Orb you use on yourself: you catch a ride on a Bullet Bill and overtake an opponent to steal 20 coins.
Uses: Use it to overtake an opponent and steal 20 coins. It also lets you pass roadblocks without triggering them, and on Faire Square, where players crowd around the central Star space, you can target them for significant coins.
Tips: It is sold only on E. Gadd's Garage and Faire Square, for 20 coins at an Orb hut (10 in a flash sale). Using one near the Star Space makes you fly past it, so do not use it right before a Star you want to buy.

sections.name: Flutter Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A green Orb that makes Flutter appear and fly you straight to the Star Space.
Uses: It can only be used on yourself. On the boards that sell it, the Star moves to a new spot after each purchase.
Tips: It costs 30 coins at an Orb hut. On Towering Treetop and E. Gadd's Garage, a Star costs 20 coins.

sections.name: Metal Mushroom Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A green Orb that turns the player who uses it into metal.
Uses: Use it before you walk through spaces where rivals have set trap Orbs. A Thwomp is deflected, a Tweester dissipates with no effect, a Podoboo attack is negated, a Bob-omb is kicked away, a Koopa Troopa gives up because you are too heavy to lift, and a Zap Orb's Amps disappear after trying to shock you.
Tips: Towering Treetop and Faire Square do not have it, which the board pages say makes roadblocks there particularly hard to avoid.

sections.name: Thwomp Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A red Orb you set on a space as a roadblock: an opponent who passes it is flattened by a Thwomp and has to stop moving.
Uses: Put it on a space your rivals must cross. On Faire Square it can stop a player from buying Stars, above all at night, when Stars may cost less, and it is often placed on the Red Space right before the fixed Star space.
Tips: It costs 10 coins at an Orb hut, or 5 in a flash sale, and is sold on Towering Treetop, Faire Square and Clockwork Castle. A rival under a Metal Mushroom Orb is not stopped, and a roadblock cannot be replaced until an opponent triggers it.

sections.name: Piranha Plant Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A yellow Orb you place on a space: an opponent who lands on it is chewed by a Piranha Plant and must give you half of their coins.
Uses: Place it on a space where rivals are likely to stop. If you land on your own space you get 5 coins, and if a rival lands there while you are standing on it, only the rival is chewed.
Tips: It costs 15 coins and is sold on every board except Towering Treetop and Castaway Bay. It affects a player who lands on the space, and it stays on the board until someone replaces it or a Star Space appears on that spot.

sections.name: Snack Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A blue Orb, sold only on Snowflake Lake, that protects you from one Chain Chomp theft.
Uses: Just carry one: you cannot use or place it, and it works by itself the first time an opponent's Chain Chomp reaches you. You throw a bone, the Chomp jumps over your space to catch it, and everyone else standing on your space is spared too. You can throw the Orb away at any time. In a team game, a Chain Chomp ride by a teammate can still use up your Snack Orb.
Tips: It costs 10 coins at an Orb hut and protects only one time, so buy another once it has been used.

sections.name: Boo-Away Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A blue Orb that stops Pink Boo from stealing from you one time; it cannot be used or placed.
Uses: Carry one on Towering Treetop or Castaway Bay and it works by itself when an opponent sends Pink Boo after you. The item inside is a flashlight, the Gaddlight of earlier games, that scares Boo away. You can throw the Orb away at any time.
Tips: It costs 10 coins at an Orb hut and is sold only on Towering Treetop and Castaway Bay, the only boards where Pink Boo appears.
